title: Level a sloping street
one_liner: Shear a plate so the ground reads flat without tipping the building over.
when: A shot reads as crooked but the verticals look fine.
how: Measure INSIDE the window the shot actually uses. Measuring across the whole plate gave 0.08 degrees here when the truth inside frame was 2.2.
If verticals are vertical and horizontals slope, it is the GROUND PLANE, so the correction is a SHEAR. A rotation would tip the building over.
Solve it iteratively - the residual after each pass is the correction still owed.

knobs.K: the shear, as ground slope (0.02445 here)
knobs.X0: the pivot column - put it on the hero building so it does not shift

gotcha: One shear cannot level a whole perspective, because lines parallel in the world converge in the image. Average the two that matter and both land inside a quarter of a degree.
